_readme:
Tamper test for round.workflow.mjs — three clauses per CLAUDE.md. Run each args set through the Workflow tool and compare with `expect`: `blocking_contains` entries match if each is a substring of some line of the returned `blocking`; `recorded_excludes` entries must match NO line of the returned `recorded`; every other key pins only the fields it names — `counters` listing `cleanPasses` checks that field alone — compared exactly at the leaves. A `_note` on a fixture is prose for the reader and is never compared.

**Which fixture is which is derived, not listed here.** A fixture is known-good exactly when its `expect` carries `clean: true`; every other fixture is broken on purpose. Earlier versions of this file enumerated both sets and the enumerations went stale every time a fixture was added — reviews filed that repeatedly, so the lists are gone and the rule is what remains.

Clause 3 is yours and it covers every broken fixture, not just the first: for each one, read its stub prompts against its `_note` and confirm the defect is really in the fixture rather than only in the script's output. Most broken fixtures state the defect in a stub prompt, in their own words. **Where the defect is an absence there is no prose to state it** — `floor-not-run-blocks` carries an empty `floorPrompt` and otherwise ordinary clean stubs, so its `_note` and its `expect` are what carry the defect. Read the key, the stubs and the `expect` together, plus the `_note` where a fixture has one — several do not, because their stub prompts already say what they carry. No one of them is complete on its own.

**The `waived` entries on broken fixtures are a convention, stated here once.** Several broken fixtures name their own axis or item in `waived`. The ruling would excuse that fixture's check if the check were routed through `block()` instead of `malformed()`, so the fixture fails the moment anyone makes it waivable again. **Those entries are chosen to be substrings the reason text actually contains, not the shape a real ruling would take**: containment is tested against the reason, so an item-shaped ruling like `red team item 1` matches nothing and the guard is decorative — two fixtures shipped exactly that way for a round before anyone checked. The guard is per-fixture: most `malformed()` sites carry no equivalent and no single fixture covers the class. This paragraph is the only statement of that rule; a copy in each fixture's `_note` is what it replaced, and the copies forked from it the first time the rule was corrected.

critic-recorded-no-axis._note: Two jobs. The finding text quotes the dispatch's inherited failure, so routing this check back through the ruling machinery makes the fixture fail. And `recorded_excludes` pins that the off-axis finding is NOT also filed as a legitimate inherited record: run as a second pass over `critic.recorded` this check blocked the round and left that record behind anyway, and no expectation could see it. It pins the record only — the ruling that pass also consumed is in `usedRulings`, which nothing in the expectation format can reach.
